tickets.title: Capture actionable, redacted failure diagnostics
tickets.action: Preserve typed cause, correlated run/attempt, start/finish, exit provenance, safe stderr/trace availability, symbolic host role, last successful run and a concrete next step. Missing historical evidence stays explicit; do not fabricate it.
tickets.acceptance: Every failed member exposes an identity-bound diagnostic envelope; synthetic error, timeout and lost-executor cases prove the fields and redaction; naturally scheduled receipt is observed after release.

tickets.title: Repair the nine observed failed jobs
tickets.action: Use the per-job causes in FAILURE_DIAGNOSTICS.md and its receipt addendum. Review the four source fixes, reuse #2444 relay changes, and investigate remaining exceptions from safely retained evidence. Protected members require their scoped grant.
tickets.acceptance: Each member has a measured subsequent attempt or explicitly documented governance block; no retry with unknown prior effects, no enforcement bypass, no success inferred from log mtime.

tickets.title: Account for six observed missed jobs
tickets.action: Trace scheduler to admission to attempt to output. Reuse #2444 for the three native relay lanes. Preserve the frozen Hermes completion-time limit and protected scalp lock boundary.
tickets.acceptance: Each member has a proven schedule and attempt/completion evidence or an owner-approved retirement/blocked disposition; no lock removal or speculative rerun.

tickets.action: Keep paused intent visible, identify the owner decision and prerequisites for each lane. Self-heal remains a separate named activation decision.
tickets.acceptance: Every paused member has current intent, owner and review date. Installing or arming requires its existing operator authority; intentional pause is never an outage.

tickets.action: Only registry and existing receipt metadata were audited. Prepare minimal generic instrumentation boundaries and request the exact engineering/operations grant before subsystem work; preserve broker/order/credential rails.
tickets.acceptance: Each protected member has a measured safe contract or explicit scope/expiry/owner decision. No broker access or live flag change is inferred from this ticket.

tickets.action: Reconcile each of eight contradictory declarations with its owner. Template instances may intentionally be unloaded; restore or retire is an owner decision.

tickets.title: Measure continuous services as services
tickets.action: Use liveness, restart/error and heartbeat contracts rather than inventing recurring cron opportunities. Preserve the distinction between healthy process and useful output.
tickets.acceptance: Every continuous service has independent liveness, freshness, error and output evidence or an explicit remediation child item.

tickets.action: Carry declared dispatch mode and observed mode into evidence. Expected nonlive output is not missing live execution; dry-run cannot prove installation.
tickets.acceptance: Every member displays intended and observed modes, real execution completion and separate business-output verdict without arming it.

tickets.title: Complete partial run contracts
tickets.action: Fill missing identity, completion, exit, output or correlation dimensions at the original writer; retain existing valid evidence.
tickets.acceptance: Every member has immutable identity-bound completion with explicit exit/output semantics, plus synthetic refusal tests and post-release evidence.

tickets.action: Reconcile each observed success with intended shadow/dry-run/preflight mode. Do not equate nonlive success with live operation.
tickets.acceptance: Each member reports execution mode, success definition and output contract; wrong/future/dry-run proof cannot establish live installation.

tickets.title: Replace modification-time evidence with run completion
tickets.action: Preserve mtime only as capture/source metadata. Reuse existing wrapper and receipt infrastructure to record identity, start, finish, exit and output.
tickets.acceptance: All members have actual completion evidence or an explicit missing instrumentation state; touching a log must not change success or last-success time.
